project.name: Validation Limitations And Future Methods
project.summary: Validation Limitations And Future Methods is a standalone literature project created from the reference layer of the supplied gene-mutation paper so that the MemoryTonic collection can contain multiple comparable projects instead of only one synthesized overview. The practical purpose of this project is to create graph structure that supports bridges, cross-paper comparison, and clearer separation between evidence types. In the original uploaded collection there was only a single project, which meant there could be no bridge entities by definition even if the research itself was thoughtful. This project addresses that structural limitation by representing one coherent slice of the cited literature as its own graph-ready unit. The focus here is: A methods-and-gaps project synthesizing the anchor paper's limitations and future directions with cited literature themes around MIL, multimodal fusion, external validation, and deployment readiness. The project therefore captures the entities, methods, validation themes, and clinically relevant concepts that recur in this part of the literature, especially histopathology images, mutation prediction, precision oncology, and the conditions under which claims should be trusted. It also encodes the difference between promising internal results and stronger external evidence. By storing this literature slice as a separate project in the same Gene Mutation Research collection, the graph can now discover which concepts are repeated across projects and which themes are unique to a single paper or subfield. That is what makes bridge entities meaningful in this platform: not a single long paper, but several connected projects that share important vocabulary, methods, datasets, and limitations.
narrative_flow: This project isolates one coherent slice of the cited gene-mutation literature so that it can function as its own graph unit inside the collection.
It focuses on recurring entities such as histopathology, mutation status, validation design, and clinically meaningful molecular targets.
The project converts those themes into structured relationships so the collection can compare methods, datasets, and claims across separate projects.
Its main value inside MemoryTonic is to create shared vocabulary with neighboring projects, enabling bridge entities and cross-paper reasoning.
Together with the other uploaded literature projects, it turns the gene-mutation collection from a single summary into a true multi-project research graph.

relationships.description: Histopathology images provide the visual substrate from which mutation-linked morphology is inferred, making tissue appearance the key non-genomic evidence source for computational mutation prediction pipelines across this literature project.
relationships.evidence: The supplied paper repeatedly frames pathology morphology as the observable phenotype of latent genomic events.

relationships.description: Somatic mutation status guides targeted therapy selection and molecular stratification in precision oncology, giving direct clinical relevance to any method that can estimate mutation state from pathology evidence.
relationships.evidence: The supplied paper describes mutation profiling as foundational to personalized cancer therapy.

relationships.description: If pathology images can support mutation inference, they become useful to precision oncology screening because they are already produced in routine care and may prioritize who most needs confirmatory sequencing.
relationships.evidence: The supplied paper frames image-based prediction as a triage and acceleration mechanism rather than only a research exercise.

relationships.description: Strong patient-level generalization is required before promising research metrics can be treated as clinically meaningful support for precision oncology workflows beyond the originating cohort.
relationships.evidence: The broader literature repeatedly distinguishes internal performance from stronger translational evidence.

relationships.description: External validation is the main empirical mechanism for establishing whether mutation-prediction systems generalize to unseen cohorts and institutions rather than only to familiar development data.
relationships.evidence: The supplied paper and its cited literature emphasize external robustness as a key standard.

relationships.description: Interpretability supports clinical trust because researchers and clinicians need to know whether a mutation prediction rests on plausible morphology or unstable artefacts before it influences precision oncology decisions.
relationships.evidence: The cited reviews identify interpretability as a major open challenge for medical AI.

relationships.description: Variation in staining, tissue composition, cohort makeup, and acquisition conditions makes patient-level generalization a central challenge for histopathology-based mutation prediction even when proof-of-concept signal exists.
relationships.evidence: The literature repeatedly returns to robustness and external validation as unresolved needs.

relationships.description: Because pathology datasets vary across institutions and cohorts, claims made from histopathology-based mutation systems require external validation to demonstrate reproducibility and real robustness.
relationships.evidence: The supplied paper highlights external validation as the stronger test across the field.

relationships.description: Image-level training can increase learnable signal and improve internal performance without automatically guaranteeing patient-level generalization, because tile-level success and new-patient robustness are not the same claim.
relationships.evidence: The anchor paper itself separates improved patch-level learning from true generalization.

relationships.description: Attention-based MIL can improve patient-level generalization by learning which regions are truly informative instead of giving every tile equal importance under coarse patient-level labels.
relationships.evidence: The supplied paper cites MIL as a future direction for addressing label noise and localization.

relationships.description: Multimodal fusion advances precision oncology by combining pathology with complementary clinical or molecular evidence, often producing stronger and more biologically informative systems than single-modality approaches.
relationships.evidence: The cited reviews summarize multimodal AI as outperforming unimodal systems on average.

relationships.description: PathGene enables stronger patient-level generalization assessment by providing benchmark infrastructure for multicentre evaluation in lung-cancer path-genomics.
relationships.evidence: The supplied paper names PathGene as a future validation target.

relationships.description: DeepGEM sets a high bar for patient-level and cohort-level robustness by pairing large multicentre scale with strong mutation-prediction performance and external testing.
relationships.evidence: The supplied paper frames DeepGEM as the top of the field for lung-cancer mutation prediction.

relationships.description: The TCGA LUAD and LUSC cohort provides paired lung-cancer histopathology data that ground and connect multiple projects in this collection, especially in early and benchmark-oriented mutation studies.
relationships.evidence: The supplied paper repeatedly uses TCGA as a foundational resource.

relationships.description: Multimodal fusion can strengthen patient-level generalization by combining complementary evidence streams, though it still requires rigorous external testing to prove robustness.
relationships.evidence: The cited reviews summarize multimodal systems as stronger on average than unimodal approaches.

relationships.description: Attention-based MIL helps localize the histopathology regions most likely to express mutation-linked morphology, offering a principled response to weak labels and region-level heterogeneity.
relationships.evidence: The supplied paper highlights MIL as a future direction for better tile relevance modeling.

causal_chains.name: Morphology To Clinical Relevance
causal_chains.description: This chain captures how pathology morphology leads to mutation prediction and then to the stricter demand for clinically meaningful validation.

links.explanation: Morphology is treated as evidence of latent genomic state.
Mutation state matters because it changes treatment reasoning.
Clinical value depends on generalization beyond the development cohort.

causal_chains.name: Validation Discipline
causal_chains.description: This chain shows why external evaluation is required before pathology mutation systems are treated as strong translational evidence.

links.explanation: Pathology claims require testing outside one data environment.
External evaluation is the main test of true generalization.
Generalization determines whether the system is useful in practice.
